Params: {3: 'Night falls over the Helio family's training ground.'}
{3: 'The other heirs have long since gone home, their training finished with the daylight. Only Adelyde remains, a lone tiny shadow in the vast room.'}
{3: 'She stands motionless, her face grave, her pistol aimed at the doorway. She has not moved in almost twenty minutes, as if awaiting something sacred.'}
{3: 'The lamp overhead is the same one that had flickered to life unprompted before. She has recreated every detail of that strange encounter.'}
{3: 'She glances down at her watch. 21:21, March 21st. Exactly as it was that night. Everything is ready.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'If you're out there, light it up again.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'She closes her eyes, lips moving in silence, mouthing the words the gray figure had left behind.'}
{3: 'Adelyde opens her eyes. Nothing stands in the doorway. Only the parterres and topiaries in her family's yard stare back at her, uncomprehending.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Disappointment settles over her. She closes her eyes again, and this time, she takes a long, deep breath.'}
{3: 'She opens her eyes, but still nothing. If the wind counts as an answer, then at least she has that much.'}
{3: 'Adelyde turns away, her face flushed with embarrassment. She is terrified someone might have heard her shouting and come to ask if she has lost her mind.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Forget it. I didn't really need you anyway.', 4: '1'}

{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde (Soldier)', 3: 'General, it seems you've found a way to turn the tide. We've been fighting alone for so long. If the mysterious soldier known as ▅ ▅ were to join our cause, we would surely claim victory.', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Soldier, you cannot rely on aid that may never arrive. Hope like that only makes you weak.', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde (Soldier)', 3: 'Then why do you keep calling that name?', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde (Soldier)', 3: 'You don't like fighting alone, do you?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'That figure might have just been in my head.', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Her mother had done the same before she lost herself, speaking to empty corners, whispering of salvation waiting in the shadows.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Adelyde feels a chill creep up her back.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'You look like you're up to something.', 4: '18'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'It looked more like you were trying to cast a spell.', 4: '18'}
{3: 'Rusalka seems to still be on a mission. Adelyde hears the sharp whistle of air rushing past, followed by the crash of bodies and scattered cries.'}

{3: 'The family calls her "Cruising Vanguard," and she has earned it. Rusalka is often sent to handle the tasks too overwhelming for anyone else. In Adelyde's eyes, what Rusalka does is mysterious, dangerous, and deeply admirable.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'What are you doing over there? Can I come with you next time?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'As they speak, Rusalka takes down several more opponents. The noise around her finally subsides.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'Enough chatter. I'm calling to let you know that the two big names have set the stage for you kids. Your trip to the Atlantic Eye is moving up.', 4: '18'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'That means you've got one month left.', 4: '18'}

{1: '1', 2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'If you hit your target, you'll be allowed to bring her home. The hospital team will become a private in-home care team. I'll handle any extra costs that come with it.', 4: '18'}
{2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'And you'll see her every week when you come back from the Atlantic Eye.', 4: '18'}
{3: 'Adelyde presses her lips together. But there is no time to savor the news. The warmth of relief barely touches her chest before her teacher moves on.'}
{3: 'The woman does not give the child a single moment to bargain. The line goes dead.'}
{3: 'One month. She needs to cover another 20 meters under full load, a distance that once took her an entire year to barely scrape past.'}
{3: 'The problem is, time is not on her side.'}

{3: 'She does not rush straight to the track. Instead, she pulls out her notebook and begins drawing, carefully mapping out force distributions. "The Atlantic Eye: Foundations of Engineering" sits open beside her.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Okay. I've got it all figured out.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'She gives a solemn little nod, doing her best impression of a tiny scholar.'}
{3: 'The truth is, Adelyde hasn't understood any of it. Not a single word.'}

{3: 'The book is filled with equations far beyond a nine-year-old. But Adelyde is not reading the math. She studies the pictures, the simple sketches of leverage and balance. And from those, she learns enough.'}
{3: 'If her body won't cooperate, her mind will.'}

{3: 'She builds a harness from spare chains and bindings, adjusting the weight distribution to ease the strain on her shoulders. The result is clumsy. The moment she loads it, she wobbles, barely holding steady.'}
{3: '83.4 meters. 82.1. 84.4. 79.1... The method works, just barely.'}

{1: '1', 3: 'Following "The Atlantic Eye: Foundations of Engineering", Adelyde rigs up a makeshift suspension point. She hoists the cross cannon with a chain, then slowly works it up to the right height before shouldering it.'}

{3: 'Best case, at 15 meters, how much longer would it take? And if she could rely on her own strength on top of her mind, how much longer would that take? The questions she had been holding back start crowding in again.'}
{3: 'A soft noise breaks the silence from behind. Crack—'}
{1: '1', 3: 'If she couldn't bring her mother back, what would be the plan going forward?'}

{3: 'She throws herself to the side just in time. A deafening crash echoes through the ground, and in the rising dust, the cross cannon sits lodged in the spot where she had been standing a moment before.'}

{3: 'Adelyde gasps. Without that sudden warning, she would be unconscious at best, or facing a broken spine and permanent disability at worst. Either way, any hope of continuing her training within thirty days would be gone.'}
{3: 'She holds her breath. That familiar gray figure, hazy but unmistakable, materializes right before her eyes.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'You're supposed to be my imagination... no, you're not my imagination...', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The sheer surrealism of it all sends Adelyde's mind into a brief overload. She springs to her feet, forcing herself to look calm.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Who are you? Where did you come from? And why are you inside Helio's training ground?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Adelyde hurls a barrage of questions, sure that she has seized control of the situation. But any onlooker would see only a small girl puffing herself up like a frightened little lynx.'}
{3: 'Now it's the phantom's turn to speak.'}
{2: 'You will meet me in the future. But in that future, we will be separated in the middle of a crisis.', 3: '244'}
{2: 'I need to find the right time to go back to where we were separated.', 3: '255'}
{3: 'The gray figure tries again and again to speak, but each time, a greater force drowns out those words before they can be heard.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'I asked you questions. Why won't you just answer?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'I can respect your choice of silence, but don't use this nonsense to mess with me.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'You don't seem like you mean me harm. So if you need help, just say so. Now—', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Rusalka appears in the doorway without a sound. Her eyes cut across the training ground, sharp and appraising, and her blade remains half-drawn. She must have rushed over as fast as she could.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'I heard a crash from halfway across the building. When I got here, I saw you talking to thin air.', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'Quite the scene you've made here, Adelyde.', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'I... I mishandled it and dropped the cross. I'll put it back.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'If anyone found out she was talking to herself, just like her mother, would they mark her as mentally broken too?'}
{3: 'The woman's face is cold and unreadable as she advances step by step. It is as if she can read exactly where Adelyde's gaze is fixed, moving straight toward the gray phantom.'}
{3: 'The phantom drifts silently toward the makeshift lifting rig and halts beside the loose chain clasp.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'She reads the shift in Adelyde's gaze and changes course at once. Her body, however, passes through the gray phantom, and she halts at the crude lifting rig.'}
{3: 'Click. With a deft flick, she snaps the loose chain clasp back into place.'}
{3: 'The long blade slides home into its sheath. Rusalka throws a brief, unreadable look behind her before turning and stepping through the doorway.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'Just making sure you weren't being threatened, Adelyde.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'Fatigue can make people see things, and it can make them vulnerable. Showing weakness is never smart.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Adelyde watches Rusalka's figure disappear through the door. Only once she is certain the woman will not turn back does she let out a long, relieved breath.'}
{3: 'She turns to the gray phantom, her eyes narrowing as the realization catches up with her.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: '...You led her there on purpose, so she'd spot the loose clasp?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The figure doesn't answer, just offering a small shrug.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Rusalka can't see you. She can't hear you either.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'But you're not my imagination... Something I made up couldn't act on its own. And it wouldn't leave my sight on purpose.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'So what are you, really? A miracle, a phantom, an alien?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Think of me as a sailor who's drifted off course.', 3: '346'}
{2: 'This isn't where I was sailing to, but somehow I ended up here.', 3: '347'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Then, where are you going? Are you looking for something?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'I'm looking for the future you.', 3: '350', 4: 'To reunite with the future you.', 5: '350'}
{3: 'The voice grows muffled and vague again. Adelyde decides not to push further. Instead, she reaches out a hand.'}
{3: 'They extend their hands toward each other, and for a moment, they almost touch. But their fingers pass straight through each other's like sand slipping through a fist.'}
{2: 'The last time I saw you, it was March 1st. Twenty days have passed.', 3: '373'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Are you saying those twenty days felt like a moment for you?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Looks like I can't control when we meet.', 3: '377'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'I know this isn't your destination, but I still have to reach mine.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'She bends down and begins dragging the cross cannon across the floor.'}
{3: 'Adelyde turns around. The phantom's lips are moving quickly, straining to tell her something. But the words never make it through, buried beneath the same muffled silence as earlier.'}
{2: '(Press your palms together, then pull them apart)', 3: '405'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'You want me to... snap it in two?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The phantom repeats the gesture. The two hands separate, then both point toward the cross cannon lodged in the floor.'}
{3: 'The gray figure nods with unmistakable, almost childlike eagerness.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'And then, an idea that's never been allowed floats up into her mind. It feels almost right.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: '...If I can't carry the whole thing, then maybe it doesn't have to be whole.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'She lowers herself to the ground and runs her fingers along the cannon's joints, hesitating to exert force. She glances up at the phantom, waiting for a sign.'}
{3: 'The figure extends a single finger and traces slowly along a nearly invisible groove.'}
{3: 'She reaches out. The clasp snaps open, and a heavy piece lurches free.'}
{3: 'What follows becomes a silent game between the two of them.'}
{3: 'With the phantom's guidance, she dismantles the weapon, a tool that grown soldiers would approach with caution, and reduces it to manageable parts.'}
{3: 'She binds each piece with chains, distributing the load across her shoulders and waist until the harness holds together, uneven but functional.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'The cross cannon, torn into fragments, is carried piece by piece. The weight has not changed by a single gram. And yet, she walks forward, one step at a time.'}
{3: 'This place allows no rest or softness. But today, for the first time in what feels like forever, the child's smile is real.'}
{2: 'You did this all by yourself, Adelyde.', 3: '462'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'But am I really carrying it... or am I just cheating my way around it?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Wisdom is also a kind of strength.', 3: '466'}
{2: 'Doing the impossible over and over, that's how you make it possible. All you need to do is—', 3: '468'}
{3: 'One step at a time, she shoulders the dismantled pieces and begins moving again.'}
{3: 'She spends the night rebuilding and breaking down the cannon, repeating the cycle until dawn breaks across the steel walls.'}
{3: 'The moment daylight comes, she calls Rusalka over. Before her teacher, she disassembles the weapon, binds the pieces to herself, and charges across the finish line with everything she has.'}
{3: 'When the run is over, she fits every piece back into place without a gap.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Rusalka stands in silence, her gaze fixed on the child who has not slept all night.'}
{2: 'Rusalka', 3: '...There are many kinds of strength. You showed me the rarest one of them all today.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'And just like that, Adelyde gets everything she has been hoping for: a real teacher and a promise that she can bring her mother home.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'We did it! It's our secret, just between you and me.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'A rare grin lights up her face. She turns to share her joy with the gray phantom, but the sight stops her cold.'}
{3: 'The morning sun cuts straight through that figure and hits the floor. The phantom's shape is growing fainter with each second, like a sketch washed away.'}
{3: 'She whirls around in panic, grabbing everything off the table: a ration bar, a sweat-soaked towel, a notebook. She shoves them into those fading hands one after another.'}
{3: 'But nothing stays. Every single item slips right through the dissolving shape like smoke through fingers.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'The first time we met, I pointed a gun at you. I never got the chance to apologize for that.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Her frantic scrambling slows, then stops altogether. She stands there, gripping the notebook of "Notes on Caring for Mom" until her knuckles turn white.'}
{3: 'The phantom lifts a hand and awkwardly curls fingers into the shape of a gun, aiming it gently at her.'}
{3: 'She tries to muster a sharp retort, but her nose betrays her with a sudden sting.'}
{2: 'It's a rehearsal for when we meet again.', 3: '543'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'A rehearsal... Will we see each other again?', 4: '18'}
{2: 'When, where, and what brings us together... I don't get to choose any of that.', 3: '549'}
{2: 'But there's one thing I do choose.', 3: '550'}
{2: 'When you feel like no one can hear that voice screaming inside you, even if I'm not beside you, I'll still be listening.', 3: '551'}
{3: 'The faint glow around the grey figure has almost faded into the morning light, yet that voice rings out with unprecedented clarity. Not a single word is swallowed by that greater force.'}
{2: 'So you hold on too... to that part of you that wants to protect something with everything it's got.', 3: '557'}
{3: 'The words crowd against her throat, but the figure has already vanished into the spreading gold.'}
{3: 'The doorway holds nothing now. Only the Helio family's parterres and topiaries remain, silent as they have always been.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Adelyde stands rooted in place for a long time.'}
{3: 'At last, she presses the little notebook against her chest, draws a deep breath, and lifts her head.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'The propellers thunder as a young Adelyde presses her face to the porthole.'}
{3: 'The clouds break open, revealing the Atlantic Eye, a vast circular edifice that spans the fiercest ocean currents, resting quietly on the water far below.'}
{3: 'Sunlight glints off the boundless metal and sea, making her eyes narrow against the glare.'}
{3: 'That place holds the strength she longs for, the acknowledgment she seeks, and a grand, protracted tale of encounters and farewells, one she is still utterly blind to.'}
{3: 'The pathway closes, and the world goes silent once again.'}
{2: '(Sort out what you've learned so far)', 3: '610'}
{3: 'You met Adelyde again twenty days later, measured by the real world. But for you, it feels like only a fleeting moment.'}
{3: 'She is the one constant in your time-lost existence, yet you cannot decide when you will see her again.'}
{3: 'If Ananke is what binds you here, then all you can do while waiting for Adelyde to enter the Atlantic Eye is offer her whatever help you can muster.'}
{2: '(...Is that all I can do? Just talk to Adelyde like today?)', 3: '614'}
{3: 'Golden strings of light gather into words before you, and ripples stir across the previously placid water.'}
{1: '"It seems I'm bound by the same order."', 3: '54'}
{2: '"It seems I'm bound by the same order."'}
{1: '"Neither of us can speak of what has not yet come to pass."', 3: '54'}
{2: '"Neither of us can speak of what has not yet come to pass."'}
{1: '"Because at this point in time, we're not meant to know the things we might say."', 3: '54'}
{2: '"Because at this point in time, we're not meant to know the things we might say."'}
{1: '"Keen perception. You must have had a great teacher."', 3: '54'}
{2: '"Keen perception. You must have had a great teacher."'}
{1: '"Your grasp is slipping. What exactly did your teacher teach you?"', 3: '54'}
{2: '"Your grasp is slipping. What exactly did your teacher teach you?"'}
{2: 'That has nothing to do with my teacher. This is my own confusion.', 3: '676', 4: 'You have no right to judge my teacher's methods.', 5: '676'}
{3: 'Maybe it's your imagination, but the angular edges of the words at the water's center seem to soften, as though pleased with your response.'}
{2: 'What should I do now?', 3: '678', 4: '(Quietly think about what to do next)', 5: '700'}
{1: '"If you are hoping to see ▅▅▅▅▅, you are welcome to keep asking questions."', 3: '54'}
{2: '"If you are hoping to see ▅▅▅▅▅, you are welcome to keep asking questions."'}
{3: 'Another question that can't be answered, it seems.'}
{1: '"Did your teacher never teach you what to do when you lose your way in the middle of a mission?"', 3: '54'}
{2: '"Did your teacher never teach you what to do when you lose your way in the middle of a mission?"'}
{3: 'When you lose your way in the middle of a mission, you should...'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'First, stay calm and trust yourself. It's not the difficulty that breaks people; it's fear and hesitation.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Second, retrace where you lost contact. The entrance to a maze can just as easily be the exit.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The instructor's voice goes silent in your head, and a bolt of lightning clears the mist.'}
{3: 'You realize it now: you fell into this place exactly when Ananke operated at full strength, spilling the golden threads into the sea. That was your way into this maze.'}
{2: 'The entrance is the exit. To leave, I need to find the moment Ananke peaks again.', 3: '722'}
{2: 'But Ananke lies at the bottom of the Atlantic Eye, and I can't even move on my own...', 3: '723'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'Your trip to the Atlantic Eye is moving up. That means you've got one month left.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'In one month, that child will step into the Atlantic Eye and move toward Ananke.'}
{3: 'You cannot choose when or where you arrive, but the other end of the light string remains fastened to her.'}
{2: 'Maybe that's where I'll find my answer.', 3: '742'}
